response.consequence: When some errors are cached and others are not, or when an error is missing from nodestore or listed twice, the replay summary sent to Seer contains errors with the wrong details, and some errors are lost. The AI summary is then built from incorrect data.
response.explanation: fetch_error_details builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, then pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` using zip. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id, not a list aligned with the input. It deduplicates the ids. Its cache-miss path (nodestore/base.py:199-205) puts the items fetched from the service first and the cached items last. It may also leave out ids that have no data. So `events.values()` can be shorter than `error_ids`, in a different order, or both. The zip then gives an event's title, message and timestamp to the wrong `id`. If an id is missing, every later error shifts onto the wrong id.
response.title: Error IDs are zipped with nodestore results by position, which misattributes or drops errors

response.consequence: Malformed reports lacking any time field are counted as valid and returned with 200. That is looser than the previous contract, and it contradicts the stated either/or rule between the two specs.
response.explanation: The old BrowserReport dataclass required `timestamp`. The new serializer makes both `age` and `timestamp` optional. The validators only reject the case where both are present, and they only run when their field is supplied. A report with neither field, such as `{"body":{},"type":"crash","url":"https://a.com","user_agent":"x","destination":"default","attempts":1}`, now passes validation. The docstrings say that exactly one must be present. Also, `initial_data.get("age")` is truthy-based, so `age: 0` together with `timestamp: 5` is accepted.
response.title: Serializer accepts reports with neither age nor timestamp

response.consequence: Every POST to the preprod artifact assemble endpoint fails with an unhandled KeyError (HTTP 500). This includes requests from orgs without the feature flag, since the call comes before the flag check. The endpoint is unusable.
response.explanation: `ProjectPreprodArtifactAssembleEndpoint.post` calls `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` before the feature-flag check. `Analytics.record` looks the event type up with `event_manager.get(...)`, which is `self._event_types[type]` and raises `KeyError` if the type is unregistered. The event is registered only as a side effect of importing `src/sentry/preprod/analytics.py`. A grep found no importer of that module: not the endpoint, not `sentry.analytics.events/__init__`, not `sentry.preprod.tasks`. `Analytics.setup` imports only `sentry.analytics.events`. The event class is therefore never registered at runtime.
response.title: Preprod analytics event is never registered; assemble endpoint raises KeyError on every request
